correctness.evidence: Clean-room enumeration generated exactly 297200 matrices. Independent Ryser evaluation reproduced the permanent distribution 17:21600, 18:216000, 20:59400, 36:200. The displayed minimizer has permanent 17, and its full row/column orbit has size 21600 and equals the entire minimum set.

originality.evidence: Targeted exact-value and exact-distribution searches located only general permanent bounds, the A001501 matrix count, and small cubic-bipartite graph censuses; no located prior source stated the 17/18/20/36 labelled permanent distribution or the one-orbit minimum.

value.evidence: At 12 vertices there are only five connected cubic bipartite graph types, plus the unique disconnected K3,3 union K3,3 type. The result is therefore an invariant table over a six-type finite universe, with no general-n theorem, structural extension, or improvement to the surrounding permanent bounds.

literature.coverage: Counts 6x6 0-1 matrices with row/column sums 3; gives 297200 at n=6 but not the permanent distribution.

literature.author: Alexander Schrijver
literature.coverage: General lower bound ((k-1)^(k-1)/k^(k-2))^n for perfect matchings/permanents.

literature.title: House of Graphs — Cubic bipartite graphs
literature.coverage: Census lists exactly five connected cubic bipartite graphs on 12 vertices.

repair.reason: Reframing as a small-order benchmark is accurate but does not meet the campaign's scientific-value threshold; a valuable repair would require a substantive generalization.

final_reason: The finite census is correct and apparently not directly tabulated in prior work, but the underlying six-isomorphism-type universe is too small and routine to support accepted-finding status without a broader theorem or structural advance.
